skill.name: skywork-search
skill.description: Search the web through the Skywork API and save source-backed result files for current research tasks.
skill.summary: Runs Skywork web searches for current, source-backed research.
skill.author: SkyworkAI

security_audit.summary: The skill implements legitimate Skywork web search, but it has significant security exposure from token caching, outbound network requests, and external browser launch commands. I found no prompt injection language, but the search script builds output filenames from raw query text and can write outside the intended temporary directory.

remediation.issue: Token cache is stored in a hidden home-directory file without visible permission hardening.
remediation.suggestion: Use an OS credential store or create the token file with mode 0600 and avoid printing full tokens.

remediation.issue: Search result filenames are derived from raw query strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use a slug, UUID, or hash for filenames and verify the final path stays inside the temporary directory.

remediation.issue: Authentication can launch a browser through subprocess, including shell=True on Windows.
remediation.suggestion: Use Python webbrowser with an allowlisted HTTPS Skywork domain and remove shell=True from the Windows path.

remediation.issue: Environment variables can change endpoints that receive token-bearing requests.
remediation.suggestion: Validate custom endpoint hosts or require explicit opt-in before sending credentials to non-default domains.

The Windows branch invokes subprocess.Popen with shell=True while passing a URL influenced by the login base configuration. That creates a higher command-injection and unsafe browser-launch risk.
The Linux branch starts xdg-open with a login URL built from the configured base URL. It is intended browser behavior, but it is still external process execution from a skill script.

semantic_findings.title: Path Traversal in Search Result Filename
semantic_findings.description: The search result path is built from the raw query string before writing the output file. A query containing slashes or an absolute path can write outside the temporary directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command-line query is directly embedded in the output filename and then opened for writing. I found no sanitization, basename check, or path containment check.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Cache Lacks Permission Hardening
semantic_findings.description: The authentication module writes token data to a hidden home-directory file without visible permission restrictions. Default file permissions may allow unintended local access to the token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token save function opens the cache file and writes JSON token data. I found no chmod, opener mode control, or operating-system credential store use near the write.

semantic_findings.title: Environment-Controlled Endpoints Receive Tokens
semantic_findings.description: Environment variables can replace the authentication or search gateway endpoints. If misconfigured, token validation or search requests can send credentials to a non-default host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The API base and gateway URL are read from the environment, and later requests include token data. This can be legitimate configuration, so confidence is high enough to flag but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Current research requests need sources beyond model training data. This skill uses the Skywork API to search the web and save source-backed results.
actual_capabilities: Authenticates with Skywork using an environment token, cached token, or browser login.
Runs one to three web search queries per command.
Sends queries to the Skywork web search gateway.
Saves each query result to a text file in a temporary directory.
Returns source URLs and snippets for later synthesis.
limitations: Requires Skywork API access and a valid token.
Limits each command to three search queries.
Uses a 30-second request timeout per query.
Caches the login token in a hidden home-directory file.

use_cases.title: Current Event Research
use_cases.description: Check recent facts, source URLs, and snippets before writing a brief.

use_cases.title: Document Source Gathering
use_cases.description: Collect web references for reports, slides, or research summaries.

use_cases.title: Technical Lookup
use_cases.description: Find current release notes, documentation pages, or issue references.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for recent information about [topic] and summarize the most reliable sources.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic] from official sources, news coverage, and expert analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [question], cite source URLs, and separate confirmed facts from uncertain claims.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Step Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Run focused searches for [topic], identify source conflicts, and produce a sourced decision brief.

output_examples.input: Search for recent battery recycling policy updates.
output_examples.output: A brief summary with source URLs, policy dates, and notes on claims that need verification.

output_examples.input: Find current documentation for a new API release.
output: Official documentation URL and version notes.
Known limitation notes from support pages.

output_examples.input: Research funding trends for climate technology.
output_examples.output: A sourced overview with recent funding numbers, major investors, and publication links.

best_practices: Use focused queries with time, location, product, or organization names.
Open and read saved result files before answering the user.
Cite source URLs when presenting factual claims.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad single-word queries for complex research.
Do not treat snippets as verified without checking source context.
Do not include sensitive private data in search queries.

faq.question: What services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Skywork authentication and web search APIs.

faq.question: Does it need credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs SKYBOT_TOKEN, a cached token, or browser login.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The script saves result text files in a temporary directory and prints their paths.

faq.question: How many queries can it run?
faq.answer: It accepts one to three queries per run.

faq.question: Does it cite sources?
faq.answer: The result files include source URLs, and the assistant should cite them in answers.

faq.question: Can it work without internet access?
faq.answer: No. It depends on Skywork API availability and network access.
